messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Problems on CmdStan 2.1.0 on Windows
parts:
[renamed subject]

Cody and Z,

Sorry to hear that the command line version isn't working. I'm currently at a conference without a good connection to a development Windows machine, so I'll try to troubleshoot without being able to verify.

First off, I'm assuming you've installed Rtools. If not, I don't have any experience with other toolchains, so you'll have to fill me in on what you're using.

@Cody, can you try that with "make -j2 bin/stanc.exe". There is a chance that the targets without .exe might not work properly.

Just in case you're wondering about the details, we use make for builds and it's not really natural to write cross-platform makefiles. At one point, we were able to use the same target under Windows and *nix, but the target may have drifted over time.


@Z, can you provide:
- version of g++
- the full output
- Windows version (mostly interested in the bitness)

I see the original error and I've only seen that on 32-bit Windows machines when the executables are compiled with the g++ shipped with Rtools on a 32-bit windows. But that doesn't rule out the possibility that the error could be encountered in some other way.

I'll apologize in advance if we don't reply immediately. We're contending with most of the Stan developers sitting in one physical location, an interesting conference, and spotty internet.



Daniel


PS. @Z, you can address me as Daniel. And I'm not a doctor.



On Mon, Jan 6, 2014 at 11:45 PM, Cody Ross <ctr...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
I am having a similar problem with installing cmd stan on Windows 7.

The "make bin/libstan.a" works, but "make -j2 bin/stanc" ends with a error:

**No rule to make 'bin/stanc'. Stop.**

Any hints?

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Problems on CmdStan 2.1.0 on Windows
parts:
Z,

First thing you need to do is type:
    make clean-all

That will clear all the artifacts (this one doesn't need BIT=32, but you can add that for consistency if you want.)

For every call to make on a 32-bit machine, you have to add BIT=32. In other words, this line is incorrect:
    >make bin/stanc.exe

You have two options

1.  Build bin/stanc.exe first.
    >make bin/stanc.exe BIT=32

(the BIT=32 can come before or after the target)

Then, you can run:
    > make BIT=32 src/models/basic_distributions/normal.exe

2. Just build the model and it'll automatically build the appropriate bin/stanc.exe. That is:
    > make BIT=32 src/models/basic_distributions/normal.exe


The error you are seeing is that the Stan compiler is being build with a 64-bit option. On the g++ line, it looks like "-m64". On a 32-bit Windows machine, that executable isn't compatible and the result is the weird characters being printed.


If that doesn't fix your problems, we'll need to dive in a little more, but I'm pretty confident that will fix your problem. It'll be slow compiling, but there isn't much if you've got limited memory.



Daniel

Hi Daniel,

"make bin/stanc.exe BIT=32" has solved the problem. Thanks very much.

Z.

On Monday, January 6, 2014 7:48:13 PM UTC-5, Daniel Lee wrote:
Z,

First thing you need to do is type:
    make clean-all

That will clear all the artifacts (this one doesn't need BIT=32, but you can add that for consistency if you want.)

For every call to make on a 32-bit machine, you have to add BIT=32. In other words, this line is incorrect:
    >make bin/stanc.exe

You have two options

1.  Build bin/stanc.exe first.
    >make bin/stanc.exe BIT=32

(the BIT=32 can come before or after the target)

Then, you can run:
    > make BIT=32 src/models/basic_distributions/normal.exe

2. Just build the model and it'll automatically build the appropriate bin/stanc.exe. That is:
    > make BIT=32 src/models/basic_distributions/normal.exe


The error you are seeing is that the Stan compiler is being build with a 64-bit option. On the g++ line, it looks like "-m64". On a 32-bit Windows machine, that executable isn't compatible and the result is the weird characters being printed.


If that doesn't fix your problems, we'll need to dive in a little more, but I'm pretty confident that will fix your problem. It'll be slow compiling, but there isn't much if you've got limited memory.



Daniel
